analysis.title: Rates Spark: Jensen who?
key_insights: Treasuries largely ignored the Nvidia-led equity rebound. The Nasdaq rallied about 6% but the 10yr yield stayed in the mid-to-low 4.9% area with a slight tendency to edge lower.
Falling oil was the bigger driver of yields. Brent dipped below $90/bbl, which should pull headline inflation lower in the December CPI releases reflecting November.
October core PCE is due Wednesday and is expected to accelerate to 3.2% YoY from 3.1%. The market should already price this, but the trend is still in the wrong direction.
Lower energy prices have less direct effect on core PCE, though some pass-through such as easing airline fares is possible.
ING maintains a cautious bond view for the next few months. Fiscal concerns in Germany (defence), France (already bloated) and the US (untamed) add risk for core bonds.
ING sees recent AI-sector sell-offs as healthy over the medium term and thinks risk could return by the turn of the year. Inflation is the big swing factor and it is too early to declare victory.
Tuesday focus: AI stock rebound, Spanish October PPI, German Ifo, US Conference Board confidence. Auctions: Netherlands €2bn 3y DSL, US $28bn 2y FRN and $70bn new 5y notes.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Expected acceleration from 3.1% is largely priced but still in the wrong direction, which supports a cautious stance on bonds.
Prior reading, which the October print is expected to exceed.
Yields held steady or edged lower despite the equity rally.
Lower oil should reduce headline inflation in December CPI releases.

risk_factors: Fiscal concerns in Germany, France and the US weighing on core bonds.
Inflation could surprise, and it is too early to declare victory.
Second-round effects in Eurozone inflation, with Spanish PPI watched.
vol_and_positioning: Treasuries showed only a brief and minor tremor from the Nvidia reversal, so bonds treated the equity move as a sideshow.

tension_points.bull_case: AI sell-offs are healthy and risk could come back on by the turn of the year, with falling oil easing headline inflation.
tension_points.bear_case: Core PCE is still accelerating and fiscal narratives in Germany, France and the US add risk for core bonds.
